title: Surface Subsidence as an Effective Indicator of Methane Emissions From Underground Coal Mines
abstract: Methane (CH4) emissions from underground coal mining remain a major and uncertain anthropogenic source. This study tests whether surface subsidence, a direct consequence of underground mining, can serve as an indicator of CH4 emissions. We use the Changzhi coal belt in Shanxi of China, a major emission hotspot, as a case study. Time‐series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar analysis of Sentinel‐1 SAR data (November 2019 to October 2024) revealed persistent subsidence across the region. Over a similar period, hyperspectral images from four satellite platforms (March 2019 to October 2024) detected 568 CH4 plumes from 33 point sources. The two data sets showed strong spatial overlap. Annual subsidence volume was significantly negatively correlated with time‐averaged point‐source emissions (r = −0.65 to −0.53, p < 0.01), indicating that subsidence, as a proxy for extracted coal volume, is a reliable indicator of cumulative emissions. Applying this hyperspectral‐calibrated relationship to areas with subsidence but no detected plumes yields total point‐source emissions of 0.288–0.508 Mt·a−1, representing 13%–43% of regional inventory estimates. Hyperspectral satellites alone miss approximately 18%–32% of this total. Combining InSAR‐derived subsidence with hyperspectral plume observations thus provides a nearly all‐weather pathway for monitoring CH4 emissions from underground coal mining.

title: A Spatiotemporal Causal Machine Learning Framework for Quantifying the Impact of PM2.5 on Asthma at the Community Level
abstract: Air pollution, particularly fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 μm or smaller (PM2.5), is a leading environmental risk factor for respiratory diseases. While previous studies have investigated the biological mechanisms linking PM2.5 to asthma exacerbation, these studies are unable to scale for population‐level assessments. In contrast, most regional analyses rely on traditional statistical models that primarily quantify associations, limiting estimation of health changes under hypothetical pollution interventions. This study introduces a spatiotemporal causal machine learning framework to estimate PM2.5‐related changes in asthma outcomes at the county level. Using county‐level monthly hospitalization and emergency department records from 2011 to 2019 in Colorado, the framework integrates spatial and temporal representation learning to model geographic interdependence and temporal dynamics in exposure–response relationships. Further, through a causal inference approach, the model estimates model‐based counterfactual health outcomes under hypothetical PM2.5 interventions, moving beyond regression‐based correlation analysis. Results show that the model‐based counterfactual estimates exhibit spatial and population heterogeneity. Larger estimated effects were observed in several communities experiencing compounded environmental and social stressors, while uncertainty was greater in data‐sparse counties.

title: Excess type I interferon disrupts developmental crosstalk and promotes premature distalization in trisomy 21 lungs
abstract:
Congenital lung anomalies are associated with Trisomy 21 lungs. Here, authors show that hyperactivation of the type I IFN signaling pathway promotes precocious epithelial cell differentiation, contributing to the T21 related lung pathologies. 
 Pulmonary complications are a primary cause of morbidity and mortality in children with Down Syndrome resulting from Trisomy 21 (T21). We recently described congenital lung anomalies associated with T21, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling is consistently hyperactivated in many T21 tissues. IFN-I is recognized as a key regulator of immune cell activation and differentiation, with an under-appreciated role in tissue development. In this study we examine the effects of over-activation and repression of IFN-I signaling in developing human lung tissues. Single-cell RNA sequencing indicates that IFN treatment of tissue explants largely recapitulates transcriptional changes associated with altered epithelial differentiation in T21 lungs. Lineage-specific cell co-culture experiments confirm that mesenchyme-driven IFN-I hyperactivation promotes epithelial bud remodeling, shifts progenitor cell identity, and suggests the induction of AT2-like programs. Our data show that IFN-I is necessary and sufficient to drive T21-related lung pathologies and provide a model system enabling therapeutic discovery. Here, authors show that hyperactivation of the type I IFN signaling pathway promotes precocious epithelial cell differentiation, contributing to the T21 related lung pathologies.

title: Spatiotemporal modulation of microalgae to boost biofuel generation from CO<sub>2</sub> by the stick-to-culture strategy
abstract:
Balancing biomass growth and lipid accumulation remains a challenge in microalgal biofuel production. Here the authors report extracellular matrix-mimicking hydrogel scaffolds that dynamically reconfigure the microenvironment of spatially organized microalgae, allowing controlled switching between the two states. 
 The accelerating global energy demand, coupled with diminishing fossil fuel reserves and growing carbon emissions, underscores the urgent need for sustainable energy solutions. Autotrophic microalgae are promising cell factories for converting CO2 into renewable biofuels. However, conventional microalgal biofuels typically depend on energy-intensive or nutrient-deficient regimes that suppress microalgal proliferation, resulting in a critical trade-off between biomass growth and lipid biosynthesis. Here, we report a separable living interface with microalgae (SLIM) platform that employs extracellular-matrix-mimicking hydrogel scaffolds to spatially organize microalgae and dynamically reconfigure their microenvironment, enabling spatiotemporal switching between biomass accumulation or lipid induction. The SLIM platform supports high-density growth of microalgae while facilitating precision substrate-driven metabolic regulation, enabling low-carbon operation and improved lipid production (8.89 g L−1). This work establishes an engineered living material that overcomes essential bottlenecks in microalgal biofuel production and offers a generalizable blueprint for biohybrid systems in advanced biomanufacturing. Here the authors report extracellular matrix-mimicking hydrogel scaffolds that dynamically reconfigure the microenvironment of spatially organized microalgae, allowing controlled switching between the two states.

title: Metabolic reprogramming modulates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy via GLS1 in chronic kidney disease in male mice
abstract:
Chronic kidney disease often causes heart enlargement, a serious complication whose mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that excess phosphate activates the metabolic enzyme GLS1, promoting heart enlargement, while blocking GLS1 protects against this effect in male mice. 
 Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is a major cardiovascular complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet its mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we show that in preclinical experiments, CKD drives cardiomyocyte metabolic reprogramming characterized by enhanced glutaminolysis and impaired oxidative phosphorylation in male C57BL/6J mice. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses identified early upregulation and activation of glutaminase 1 (GLS1) in CKD hearts, while serum-induced GLS1 activity was associated with LV hypertrophic remodeling in a multicenter peritoneal dialysis cohort. Human myocardial samples also showed increased GLS1 expression in CKD. Cardiomyocyte-specific deletion or pharmacological inhibition of GLS1 attenuated CKD-induced hypertrophy in these mouse models. Proteomic and mechanistic analyses further identified phosphate as a major regulator of GLS1 activity and expression. Excessive GLS1 activation increased ammonia production, disrupted mitochondrial respiratory protein expression and redox homeostasis, and reduced bioenergetic efficiency. These findings identify a phosphate–GLS1–glutaminolysis axis linking the uremic milieu to mitochondrial dysfunction and cardiac hypertrophy, and suggest GLS1 as a potential therapeutic target for CKD-associated LVH. title: The gene ivory:mir-193 controls scale type differentiation in Heliconius butterflies
abstract:
Butterfly wing scales are diverse cell types that generate the colours and structures used in communication and adaptation. This study shows that the non-coding RNA ‘ivory’ controls alternative scale-cell states, linking regulatory evolution to phenotypic diversity. 
 The ivory:mir-193 locus is a genetic hotspot underlying melanic wing pattern variation across Lepidoptera, acting as a master regulator of melanic scale fate. This includes the genus Heliconius, where aposematic mimicry is driven by three scale cell types: light Type I, dark-melanic Type II, and red Type III scales. We test functions of ivory:mir-193 in Heliconius using CRISPR-induced somatic mosaic knockouts of ivory and mir-193 across multiple pattern morphs. Knockouts convert Type II scales to Type I scales. Effects on Type III scales vary among and within individuals, indicating that ivory:mir-193 is permissive for Type III development. Using single-nucleus RNA-seq, we profile the transcriptional landscape of H. melpomene Δ78k mutants lacking mir-193. Loss of mir-193 produces readthrough transcription, consistent with a model where mir-193 acts as a co-transcriptional terminator. These data show that miR-193, a miRNA under the transcriptional control of the ivory host gene, mediate the diversification of wing patterns across Lepidoptera by modulating scale cell identity during pupal wing development. This study shows that the non-coding RNA ‘ivory’ controls alternative scale-cell states, linking regulatory evolution to phenotypic diversity.

title: Li<sup>+</sup>-locked domain effect for breaking the temperature stability bottleneck in thermal-detection high-entropy energy storage ceramics
abstract:
Dielectric energy-storage ceramics lose polarization at high temperatures, limiting harsh-environment use. Here, the authors show a Li+- locked domain effect in high-entropy BNT-based ceramics, achieving Wrec = 11.43 J cm−3, η = 84.67%, Δη/η < 0.3% up to 320 °C, with self-diagnostic thermometry. 
 Conventional brain pacemakers rely on electrochemical batteries, which suffer from leakage, performance degradation, and neurotoxicity, posing serious safety risks. Ceramic-based pulse generators with ultra-fast discharge, high-temperature stability, and self-diagnostic capability offer a promising alternative. However, most dielectric ceramics lose their polarization activity at elevated temperatures. To address this challenge, we introduce a high-entropy composition design that induces a Li-locked domain effect in the ceramic system (1-x)[0.9(Bi0.47Na0.47Yb0.03Tm0.01)TiO3−0.1LiTaO3]−0.06(Ba0.3Sr0.7)(Sn0.5Hf0.5)O3. We demonstrate that Li+-enriched regions lock polar nanodomains, preserving them even at 300 °C. This mechanism yields a recoverable energy density of 11.43 J·cm−3, an efficiency of 84.67%, and excellent temperature stability (Δη/η < 0.3% up to 320 °C). Moreover, Yb3+/Tm3+ co-doping enables anomalous thermal enhancement of photoluminescence and precise temperature monitoring. Remarkably, the experimentally measured temperature sensing deviation is only ±0.23 K. The integration of stable energy storage and optical self-diagnosis provides a new paradigm for ceramic-based brain pacemaker pulse generators with early warning capability, pointing toward a possible solution to the intrinsic safety limitations of conventional battery-powered devices. title: Volumetric scattering microscopy
abstract:
Volumetric scattering microscopy (VSM) enables non-invasive and scan-free 3D fluorescence imaging through scattering biological tissues, allowing clearer visualization across multiple scales, including cells, tissues, and intact organisms. 
 Optical scattering in biological tissues fundamentally limits fluorescence imaging by disrupting spatial and angular information, thereby restricting volumetric visualization. Although hardware-intensive and computational approaches have advanced scattering microscopy, practical three-dimensional imaging through tissue remains constrained by instrumental complexity and axial ambiguity. Here, we present volumetric scattering microscopy (VSM), a scan-free, optical–computational framework for three-dimensional fluorescence imaging in scattering biological media. VSM captures angularly resolved speckle-encoded fluorescence using an aperture-segmented Fourier light-field configuration and reconstructs volumetric structure through adaptive feature-based descattering and joint sub-pupil alignment. This hybrid strategy preserves angular information embedded in scattered light without wavefront measurement or mechanical scanning, while maintaining the simplicity of a standard epi-fluorescence architecture. We demonstrate high-fidelity volumetric reconstruction across phantoms, engineered cellular systems, ex vivo tissues with volumetric muscle loss, and intact Xenopus embryos, achieving preserved spatial resolution, enhanced optical sectioning, and quantitative accuracy under strong scattering conditions. VSM supports large-field, robust volumetric imaging in both layered and fully embedded scattering environments. By transforming scattered light into a structured encoding resource, VSM establishes a scalable pathway toward routine three-dimensional fluorescence imaging in complex biological systems. Volumetric scattering microscopy (VSM) enables non-invasive and scan-free 3D fluorescence imaging through scattering biological tissues, allowing clearer visualization across multiple scales, including cells, tissues, and intact organisms.

title: Small-molecule targeting of kinesin-13 KIF2C enhances double-strand break DNA repair and slows down aging
abstract:
DNA damage is associated with aging and premature aging disorders. Here, the authors show that small molecule activation of the kinesin-13 KIF2C improves double-strand break DNA repair in aged cells and extends lifespan in progeria mice. 
 DNA damage is a central driver of the aging process. We previously found that the kinesin-13 KIF2C, shown to play a role in DNA repair, is repressed in aged cells. Here, we investigate whether increased KIF2C activity can counteract DNA damage and alleviate aging-related phenotypes. We demonstrate that a small-molecule agonist of KIF2C enhances DNA repair in two distinct genetic disorders characterized by pervasive DNA damage and accelerated aging: the Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) and the Down syndrome (DS). Mechanistically, the KIF2C agonist improves double-strand break (DSB) DNA repair in aged and patient-derived cells by restoring the assembly of nuclear envelope invaginations driven by cytoplasmic microtubules. Enhanced DSB DNA repair in HGPS and DS cells translates into amended nuclear structure and transcriptional signatures. Moreover, subcutaneous administration of the KIF2C agonist in progeria mice mitigates aging phenotypes and extends both health and lifespan. Our study discloses a geroprotective pharmacological approach that acts by hindering DSB DNA damage, and thus we demonstrate that enhanced genome stability can delay aging. title: PRMT1 methylates SKP1 to inhibit the ubiquitination of pro-proliferative phosphoproteins during hepatocyte proliferation
abstract:
During liver regeneration, EGF upregulates PRMT1, leading to increased asymmetric arginine dimethylation at R81 of SKP1. This impedes the interaction between SKP1 and FBXW7, protects pro-proliferative phosphoproteins from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, and thereby maintains hepatocyte proliferation. 
 Protein phosphorylation cascades are essential for cell proliferation. Here, we identify protein arginine methyltransferase 1 (PRMT1) as a key stabilizer of phosphoproteins that is indispensable for hepatocyte proliferation during liver regeneration. PRMT1 is upregulated by epidermal growth factor (EGF) via receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and catalyzes the asymmetric dimethylation (ADMA) modification of SKP1 at the R81 residue. This methylation event disrupts FBXW7 recruitment to the SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein (SCF) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, thereby preventing FBXW7-mediated ubiquitination. Since FBXW7 targets multiple pro-proliferative phosphoproteins, this mechanism prevents their degradation, ensuring the transduction of proliferative signals via phosphorylation cascades. Furthermore, in vivo administration of S-adenosylmethionine, the methyl donor for PRMT-catalyzed methylation, significantly accelerates liver regeneration in both mice and patients. Collectively, these findings establish PRMT1 as a central post-translational regulator of hepatocyte proliferation, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for liver diseases. This impedes the interaction between SKP1 and FBXW7, protects pro-proliferative phosphoproteins from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, and thereby maintains hepatocyte proliferation.

title: Polar front jet regulates tropical sea surface temperature impacts on South China extreme precipitation
abstract:
Record precipitation over South China in April–May 2024 resulted from low-level moisture convergence associated with a trough between two anomalous anticyclones, according to statistical diagnostics and model simulations. 
 Extreme precipitation over South China is commonly attributed to tropical sea surface temperature forcing, yet the role of extratropical circulation remains unclear. Using observational and reanalysis data, Rossby wave propagation diagnostics and numerical experiments, we investigate record-breaking April–May 2024 rainfall. Here we show that a trough between anomalous anticyclones over the tropical western North Pacific and Northeast Asia drives moisture convergence over South China. The tropical anticyclone enhanced moisture transport into South China, whereas the Northeast Asian anticyclone suppressed moisture export, favoring moisture accumulation. While the tropical anticyclone was forced by Indian Ocean sea surface temperature anomalies, the Northeast Asian anticyclone developed within a midlatitude Rossby wave train initiated by tropical Atlantic convection and guided by a transient eddy-driven polar front jet. European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts model reproduced tropical forcing but underestimated precipitation because of the polar front jet biases. These findings highlight the importance of extratropical flow for predicting tropical-forced extremes. Record precipitation over South China in April–May 2024 resulted from low-level moisture convergence associated with a trough between two anomalous anticyclones, according to statistical diagnostics and model simulations.

title: Distinct intraseasonal pathways driving rapidly escalating heat extremes in North China and their subseasonal predictability
abstract:
Rapidly escalating heat extremes in North China are classified into four types with distinct intraseasonal physical pathways, with tropical-driven events showing the highest predictability and dual-extratropical-wave-train events the lowest, as revealed by observations and climate model experiments. 
 Rapidly escalating heat extremes, characterized by abrupt onset and limited preparation time, pose disproportionate risks to public health, agriculture, and regional economies, yet their governing mechanisms and subseasonal predictability remain poorly understood. Here we identify 107 such events over North China during the summers of 1940–2024 and classify them into four spatial types. Thermodynamic and circulation analyses show that rapid warming arises from different combinations of horizontal warm advection and subsidence-induced adiabatic heating. The four types are linked to distinct intraseasonal circulation patterns involving tropical convection, mid–high-latitude wave trains, or their interference. Forecasts from subseasonal-to-seasonal dynamical prediction systems show a consistent hierarchy: events driven mainly by tropical intraseasonal variability are the most predictable, whereas events associated with two extratropical wave trains have the lowest skill. These results establish a process-based framework linking intraseasonal dynamics to rapid heat escalation and provide a physical basis for improving subseasonal prediction of high-impact heat extremes.
